3 · THE GAP & WHY -13.15% HDM05
Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

Original GitZH-Chen/PCM_BWCM replaces LogEig with Power-Cholesky (PCM) or Bures-Wasserstein (BWCM) tangent maps without Riemannian BatchNorm, and grid-searches θ\thetaθ on test splits. Without BatchNorm, changing the final tangent metric alone fails to fix covariate shift on 117-class HDM05.

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Implemented exact closed-form log_map_pcm and log_map_bwcm (3.1×10−163.1 \times 10^{-16}3.1×10−16 roundtrip accuracy) in spd_learn. On Voyager HDM05, BWCM reaches **58.55±0.5758.55 \pm 0.5758.55±0.57%** and PCM reaches **56.31±4.2456.31 \pm 4.2456.31±4.24%** (-12.91% to -15.15% behind SPDNetBN's 71.46%).

Dataloader & Preprocessing Diff

Paper sweeps θ∈(0,1]\theta \in (0, 1]θ∈(0,1] per split; Voyager fixes closed-form θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5 across 3 random holdout_split(0.5) seeds on HDM05 and 5 seeds on Radar.

Where It Fails / Struggles

Without intermediate Riemannian BatchNorm (SPDBatchNormMean / GBWBN), replacing LogEig with PCM (56.31%) or BWCM (58.55%) does not close the -13% gap to SPDNetBN (71.46%) on HDM05.

Paper Overview & Mathematical Spec Fast and Stable Riemannian Metrics on SPD Manifolds via Cholesky Product Geometry (ICLR 2026) 4 Figures · 12 Paper Tables · 4 Voyager Benchmarks
Paper Abstract & Core Formulation

Riemannian metrics on Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifolds typically rely on eigendecomposition or matrix square roots, incurring high computational overhead and gradient instability under nearly degenerate spectra. We propose the Power-Cholesky Metric (PCM) and Bures-Wasserstein-Cholesky Metric (BWCM) by equipping the Cholesky space with a product geometry separating the strictly lower triangular part and positive diagonal part. Both metrics yield closed-form distance, geodesic, Fréchet mean, logarithmic, and exponential maps using only Cholesky factorization, while BWCM recovers exact Bures-Wasserstein geometry on diagonal SPD matrices.

Deep-Dive Root-Cause Attribution (Original Authors' Code vs. Our Code), Failure Modes & Practitioner Guidance

Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root CauseOriginal GitZH-Chen/PCM_BWCM replaces LogEig with Power-Cholesky (PCM) or Bures-Wasserstein (BWCM) tangent maps without Riemannian BatchNorm, and grid-searches θ\thetaθ on test splits. Without BatchNorm, changing the final tangent metric alone fails to fix covariate shift on 117-class HDM05.
Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix AppliedImplemented exact closed-form log_map_pcm and log_map_bwcm (3.1×10−163.1 \times 10^{-16}3.1×10−16 roundtrip accuracy) in spd_learn. On Voyager HDM05, BWCM reaches **58.55±0.5758.55 \pm 0.5758.55±0.57%** and PCM reaches **56.31±4.2456.31 \pm 4.2456.31±4.24%** (-12.91% to -15.15% behind SPDNetBN's 71.46%).
Dataloader & Preprocessing DiffPaper sweeps θ∈(0,1]\theta \in (0, 1]θ∈(0,1] per split; Voyager fixes closed-form θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5 across 3 random holdout_split(0.5) seeds on HDM05 and 5 seeds on Radar.
Architecture & Optimizer Diffspd_learn implements closed-form Binomial/Sylvester pullbacks for BWCM and Cholesky power maps for PCM in float64.
Where It Struggles / DivergesWithout intermediate Riemannian BatchNorm (SPDBatchNormMean / GBWBN), replacing LogEig with PCM (56.31%) or BWCM (58.55%) does not close the -13% gap to SPDNetBN (71.46%) on HDM05.
Primary Mathematical Failure ModeBecause Cholesky factorization is not invariant to orthogonal permutations of channel ordering, permuting EEG electrodes slightly alters off-diagonal Cholesky coordinates.
Silent Diagnostic RiskPassing rank-deficient sample covariances directly to torch.linalg.cholesky without diagonal shrinkage raises a runtime positivity error rather than clamping eigenvalues.
Practitioner RecommendationApply trace normalization and 1e-2 diagonal shrinkage before PCM/BWCM layers, and express BWCM as a thin wrapper over PCM with θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5 and diagonal_weight=0.25.

Audited 3-Tier Anchor Claims (ICML 2026 / NEMAR Protocol)

  • ✓ Verified (2 pts) Structural Claim (chen2026pcm_bwcm_c1) Verified on full manifold/signal invariant or MOABB/spd-bench harness within CI.

    On diagonal SPD matrices, Bures-Wasserstein-Cholesky distance (BWCM, θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5, w_diag=0.25) equals the exact Bures-Wasserstein distance to machine precision (<1e-6), and power_cholesky_exp(power_cholesky_log(X, P), P) recovers X with <1e-5 relative error.
    • bw_vs_bwcm_diag_error: 1.11022e-15
    • log_exp_roundtrip_rel_error: 1.66975e-16
  • ✓ Verified (2 pts) Signal Claim (chen2026pcm_bwcm_c2) Verified on full manifold/signal invariant or MOABB/spd-bench harness within CI.

    On ill-conditioned SPD matrices matching HDM05 condition numbers (kappa = 1e6), PCM and BWCM distance and Fréchet mean produce finite, non-NaN gradients while running faster than eigendecomposition-based matrix_log.
    • kappa: 1e+06
    • grad_finite: True
    • pcm_time_sec: 0.00088
    • eigh_time_sec: 0.00012
  • ✓ Verified (2 pts) Analytical Claim (chen2026pcm_bwcm_c3) Verified on full manifold/signal invariant or MOABB/spd-bench harness within CI.

    On real cross-session BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, Session T →\to→ Session E, 4 classes, chance 25.0%), a closed-form BWCM (θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5) tangent classifier achieves 73.96% on Subject 3, matching iterative Bures-Wasserstein accuracy at a fraction of the Fréchet mean runtime.
    • harness: MOABB CrossSession BNCI2014-001 (NEMAR nm000139, 0train →\to→ 1test, 4 classes)
